title: participatory-rollout-cadence-and-ops-notes-wip
body:
Purpose

This is a working sketch for a participatory rollout cadence that explicitly brings customer-facing teams (CS/Support/Success), SRE, Product, Observability, and Solutions Eng into the canary/A-B loop. The goal: reduce blindspots during early exposure, accelerate high-confidence signal collection, and create clear human handoffs for whitelisting/opt-ins. Focus is on low-latency features and routing-sensitive LLM endpoints where cost and latency tradeoffs matter.

Context and motivation
- We have lots of technical canary playbooks (traffic slicing, telemetry hooks) but fewer operational rituals that surface customer impact early.
- When canaries show subtle quality regressions (semantic drift, hallucination rate), CS is often surprised because tech signals look healthy (latency/500s).
- Participatory rollout = short ceremonies + curated cohort recruit + live feedback channel + explicit acceptance gates.

High-level cadence (2-week sprint friendly)
1) Pre-slice week (Day -7 to -3)
   - Stakeholders aligned: Product PM, Feature Owner, SRE oncall, CS lead, Observability eng, Solutions Eng.
   - Create cohort definitions: internal-devs, opt-in beta customers, synthetic-agents (1000 req/min), ramp thresholds.
   - Quick acceptance criteria draft: user-facing metric targets (NPS conversation score delta <= 1.5), error budget impact (<5% additional 5xx), P95 latency delta (<20ms).
   - Ship prerelease note: internal docs + CS playbook for talking points.

2) Activation day (Day 0)
   - Canary opens to internal-dev cohort (1% traffic). Observe 1–2h for infra and SLO signals.
   - Stakeholder check-in call (15min) at +2h. Quick decision: proceed/hold/rollback.
   - If green, expand to opt-in beta customers (5% traffic) with explicit consent email from CS. Create live Google Sheet for notes.

3) Observational window (Day 0 to Day 3)
   - Measurement streams: latency SLOs, cost-per-request proxy, quality checks (prompt set pass rate), human flags (customer complaints), regression eval snapshots.
   - SRE/observability to run synthetic stress at off-peak for capacity guardrails.
   - CS organizes 24–48h proactive outreach to opt-in customers: scripted questions (see CS script below). Capture responses as structured tags (positive/neutral/negative).

4) Decision & crossfunc review (Day 3)
   - 30–45min review meeting. Report: signal summary, top incidents, customer anecdote, cost delta estimate. Decision options: ramp, hold-and-fix, rollback.
   - If ramping, choose increment (to 25% -> 50% -> full) tied to metric thresholds and timeboxes.

5) Postmortem & playbook update (after stabilization)
   - 1-week doc of lessons, update automated checks, add any new prompt-set tests to regression harness.

Rituals and human roles (short)
- Rollout Steward (product lead) — keeper of the hypothesis, chairs the activation & review calls, signs off final ramp.
- Signal Owner (observability) — maintains dashboard & synthetic probes; runs quick cohort dives.
- Customer Steward (CS lead) — assembles opt-in list, surfaces earliest customer comments, triggers targeted outreach.
- SRE Guard (oncall) — empowered to pause traffic based on infra thresholds.
- Solutions Eng — runs targeted QA with high-value customer inputs, validates prompt templates.

Customer outreach script (CS) — short checklist
- Quick context sentence about feature and opt-in specifics.
- 3 focused questions (did the result meet expectations? any safety/accuracy issues? did latency affect your workflow?).
- Ask for a 1–2 sentence example if they report a problem.
- Collect consent to be contacted for follow-up.

Safety & rollback heuristics
- Hard stop if: >1% of opt-in customers file a severity-2 complaint within 24h, or any P95 latency spike >2x baselined, or sustained model quality drop >10% on the evaluation prompt set.
- Soft hold if: increased error rates without user-visible complaints — require triage and extended observation window.

A/B considerations inside participatory flow
- Always pre-register primary metric and delta that would be considered wins/loses (e.g., rerank CTR, completion coherence score).
- For small opt-in cohorts, prefer paired comparisons and within-customer designs where possible to reduce variance.
- Power: for conversational metrics with high variance, use stronger signal aggregation (session-level smoothing) and accept longer observation windows.

Telemetry and dashboards (practical)
- Minimal dashboard should include: cohort allocation, P50/P90/P95 latency, 5xx rate, tokens-per-request change, model output quality pass rate (regression prompts), human flags count.
- Add customer sentiment panel that compiles CS tags into a rolling score.

Playbook templates (copy-paste)
- Activation checklist (quick): canary key, activation script, rollback command, slack channel, page URLs, contact list.
- Review agenda (30min): quick signal summary (5m), top incidents (5m), customer snapshot (5m), recommendation & vote (15m).

Open questions / follow-ups
- How do we scale participatory rollouts for small features that touch thousands of customers but have low risk? Leaner ceremony or automated gating?
- Can we integrate a lightweight consent UI into the Console that marks customers as "opt-in canary" and automates email + sheet population? Product ops to evaluate.
- Should we add a dedicated customer feedback webhook that CS can subscribe to (structured JSON) for faster ingestion?

Quick notes and links
- Related: Confluence page with regression prompt sets (see linked artifacts).
- Proto dashboard: /dashboards/rollouts/participatory-canary-preview (observability owns).
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-playbooks/pull/92 (contains a sample activation script).

Immediate next steps (owner: Jordan Li)
- Run a dry-rehearsal with internal developer cohort next sprint (target: 2026-02-16). Invite CS reps + SRE oncall.
- Solve the intake sheet template and post to Confluence.
- Draft a short-console checkbox UX proposal for opt-in cohorts (work with devx).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep ceremony short. Human attention is the scarce resource. Aim for 15–30min synchronous checkpoints, 5–10min async updates.
- Emphasize customer storytelling; anecdote + metric often better for biz stakeholders than raw charts.

-- end of sketch --
